en: The Philippine flag is the only national flag globally that is flown with the red stripe on top during a state of war.
Julian Felipe composed the Philippine national anthem in 1898 as an instrumental march, and it only received its official lyrics years later.
The Philippine Declaration of Independence was originally written in Spanish and signed by 98 people, remarkably including an American army officer.
The President of the Philippines can declare martial law, but the Constitution strictly limits this period to a maximum of sixty days.
The Philippine Constitution uniquely mandates that the State must protect and promote the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology.
The MassKara Festival in Bacolod City was created in 1980 to lift the spirits of locals during a severe sugar industry crisis.
The T'boli people of South Cotabato weave the intricate T'nalak cloth from abaca fibers using a traditional process where designs are revealed in dreams.
Baybayin is an ancient pre-colonial Philippine writing system where each consonant-vowel syllable is represented by a single unique character instead of an alphabet.
The Filipino value of bayanihan originated from the tradition of community members physically carrying an entire nipa hut on bamboo poles to a new location.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a makeshift incubator using two nested bamboo baskets to keep newborns warm in rural areas without electricity.
National Artist Juan Luna painted the massive historical masterpiece Spoliarium, which won the first gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts.
Apolinario Mabini, known as the Brains of the Revolution, continued advising the Philippine government while completely paralyzed by polio.
